SELECTED_INDEX: 10
CONFIDENCE: 0.33
EXPLANATION: The intense Raman line at 2273 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of a ν(C≡N) stretch, so a nitrile-containing candidate is required; only 4, 6 and 10 have a C≡N group.  The spectrum also shows two strong carbonyl bands at 1744 and 1782 cm⁻¹, typical of a carbonate / lactone C=O rather than an amide or imidate (which appear lower, ~1650–1720 cm⁻¹).  Among the nitrile-bearing candidates, only 10 (N#CCc1coc(=O)o1) contains a carbonate-type lactone carbonyl able to give the observed doublet near 1750–1780 cm⁻¹.  Additional supporting matches are:

• Aromatic ring stretches at 1508, 1538 and 1639 cm⁻¹, consistent with the benzofused dioxol-one ring in 10, whereas 4 and 6 lack an aromatic system.  
• Strong band at 894 cm⁻¹ matches the characteristic C–H out-of-plane bending of a 1,2,3-trisubstituted benzene ring as found in 10.  
• Bands at 1218 and 1239 cm⁻¹ correspond to C–O–C stretches of the dioxolane ring and carbonate group present only in 10.  
• Aliphatic C–H stretches at 2939 and 2972 cm⁻¹ are compatible with the –CH₂– group linking the nitrile to the aromatic ring in 10.

Taken together, the simultaneous presence of a nitrile (2273 cm⁻¹), carbonate/lactone carbonyl doublet (~1740–1780 cm⁻¹), aromatic ring modes, and C–O stretches uniquely support candidate 10 over the other options.
